brief: A caddy for next to my kitchen sink: a dispenser that pours out bleach for wiping the counters, plus two bins for sponges.

requirements.requirement: Caddy for next to the kitchen sink
requirements.evidence: Built a compact two-cell caddy (piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full, capped with capOpenFaces and bolted with lockJoints, check_build clear). It is a sink-side holder only; the bleach-dispensing function is not included, so the overall brief is only partly covered.

requirements.requirement: A dispenser that pours out bleach for wiping the counters
requirements.evidence: Not built. No dispenser/pouring part exists in the catalog (find_parts for dispenser/bottle/pour returned nothing), and a 3D-printed plastic vessel holding and pouring bleach cannot be verified here: the configurator checks fit only and knows nothing about chemical resistance, sealing or material safety. Holding/pouring bleach in printed plastic as asked is unsafe/unverifiable, so no bleach container was made. Use a commercially rated bleach bottle/dispenser kept beside (not in) this caddy instead.

Two separate drained bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, one in each cell. The drained floors suit wet sponges by letting water escape rather than pooling (shape only; waterproofing/material performance is not verified by the configurator).

finish.summary: Built the safe part of the brief: a two-cell sink-side caddy with two drained sponge bins, capped and joint-locked, verified clear by check_build. The bleach dispenser was not built — there is no dispensing part, and bleach storage/pouring in 3D-printed plastic cannot be verified for chemical resistance or sealing — so that requirement is reported unmet and the outcome is a compromise.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
